hero.headline: Trump floats federal stake in AI companies to share profits with public
hero.body:
President Trump has proposed that the U.S. government acquire small ownership stakes in major artificial intelligence companies, allowing the American public to benefit financially from what he expects will become trillion-dollar enterprises.

"There's something very interesting about it, where it almost becomes a partnership with the American public," Trump said to reporters aboard Air Force One. "It's like you make them [partners] in this revolution. It would be a beautiful thing. ... It would make 'em rich."

Trump indicated he has raised the concept during recent meetings with AI company leaders, describing their reactions as surprised. The idea would represent a significant shift from traditional government-industry relationships, establishing direct financial connections between federal authorities and private technology firms developing artificial intelligence.

The proposal aligns with existing advocacy from influential figures in the tech sector. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has previously championed similar arrangements. This week, Senator Bernie Sanders revived the discussion by proposing that the public receive a direct ownership stake in major AI companies through a one-time 50 percent tax paid in stock.

The concept raises several unresolved questions about practical implementation. Details remain unclear regarding how ownership stakes would be structured, what percentage of companies the government would acquire, and the mechanisms for distributing any resulting profits to taxpayers. Trump has not specified whether he would pursue the idea through executive action or request congressional approval.

The timing of Trump's suggestion comes as artificial intelligence companies have attracted enormous investment and as policymakers grapple with regulating the rapidly advancing technology. The notion of federal ownership in private AI firms introduces potential complications, particularly regarding the government's multiple roles as investor, regulator, and national security overseer of the industry.

Federal ownership stakes could create significant conflicts of interest. The government would need to balance its financial interests in company growth and profitability against its regulatory responsibilities and obligations to protect national security. These competing interests might affect policy decisions related to AI development, safety standards, and international competitiveness.

The proposal also raises governance questions about how the government would exercise its ownership stake and whether federal representatives would serve on company boards. Such involvement could influence strategic decisions at some of the world's most important technology companies.

Industry observers note that the concept differs from traditional government support mechanisms like grants or tax incentives. It would tie public finances directly to the success of specific private companies, creating unprecedented arrangements in the technology sector.

As AI technology continues advancing rapidly and companies in the space command increasing valuations, the conversation about how the public should benefit from this growth appears likely to intensify. Trump's public endorsement of the idea suggests it may receive serious consideration within his administration going forward.

cards.headline: Screwworm parasite detected in Texas prompts border closure and emergency response
cards.body:
A flesh-eating parasite that had not been confirmed in the United States for nearly 60 years has been found in a calf in south Texas, about 50 miles from the Mexico border. The discovery of the New World screwworm fly has triggered an emergency response from federal and state agricultural authorities and prompted neighboring countries to restrict cattle imports.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins announced the detection late on Wednesday, marking the first confirmed case in Texas since 1966. The parasite, whose larvae feed on the blood and tissue of warm-blooded animals, was eradicated from the United States in the 1970s after causing tens of millions of dollars in losses. Federal and Texas officials had warned livestock owners for more than a year about the parasite's progression through Mexico, where it advanced more than 1,100 miles northward.

The discovery has raised significant concerns for the cattle industry at a time when beef prices are at record highs. While the flies pose no direct threat to food safety, officials worry that an established population could cause shortages if the infestation spreads among cattle and poultry operations. A second infected calf was subsequently identified, and Texas declared a state of disaster over the outbreak.

Canada has responded by banning cattle imports from Texas in response to the outbreak. The movement restrictions reflect concerns about the parasite's potential to establish itself in North America if containment efforts fail.

Rollins stated that "there is no threat of mass infestation" and expressed confidence that the detection would not lead to widespread establishment of the pest in the country. However, Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller criticized the USDA's response strategy, noting that despite the release of billions of sterile flies, the screwworm had continued advancing toward Texas. Miller called for increased deployment of the screwworm adult suppression system, which uses attractants, bait, and targeted insecticides to reduce adult fly populations before sterile fly releases complete the eradication effort.

The USDA is leading containment efforts with support from the Army Corps of Engineers. In March, the agency announced construction of a new sterile fly production facility at Moore Airbase in Edinburg, Texas, to boost the response. The sterile fly approach has proven effective in previous eradication campaigns, as female screwworm flies mate only once in their lifetime, and eggs from sterile males do not hatch.

This detection comes after an isolated case confirmed in a Maryland resident who had traveled to El Salvador in August 2025, though that individual recovered with no further transmission. The last significant outbreak occurred in the Florida Keys in September 2016, mostly affecting wild deer, and was contained early the following year without spreading further.

cards.headline: Israeli Strike Kills Three Lebanese Soldiers Days After Truce
cards.teaser: Three Lebanese soldiers were killed in an Israeli strike just days after a ceasefire agreement was signed.
cards.body:
An Israeli military strike killed three Lebanese army officers shortly after Israel and Hezbollah agreed to a ceasefire. The Israeli military confirmed hitting a vehicle in the incident, which is under review.

Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun condemned the strike as "a flagrant violation to Lebanese sovereignty and international law." The incident raises concerns about the ceasefire's stability, as Israel's military operations in Lebanon have increasingly involved Lebanese state forces alongside its primary focus on combating Hezbollah, an Iran-backed armed group.

cards.headline: Ukraine Launches Drone Strikes on St. Petersburg
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces targeted St. Petersburg with drones in what Russian officials described as an unprecedented attack.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck military facilities in St. Petersburg, prompting the city's governor to urge residents to remain indoors—the first such directive since the war began. Russia characterized the attacks as "unprecedented" in scale.

The strikes targeted cargo ships and military installations in the Sea of Azov and Russian-occupied coastal waters. The operation came after Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's offer for direct negotiations.

cards.headline: Supreme Court nears decisions on birthright citizenship and presidential power
cards.teaser: The court will rule in coming weeks on cases affecting immigration policy and executive authority over federal officials.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court is preparing to issue decisions in several major cases before its summer recess. The pending rulings include challenges to birthright citizenship policies, immigration enforcement, and the extent of presidential power to remove federal employees from their positions.

The cases represent some of the court's most significant decisions of the term. The rulings will affect constitutional questions surrounding immigration policy and the separation of powers between branches of government. The court typically completes its work by late June or early July.

cards.headline: Trump agenda faces resistance from courts and Republican lawmakers
cards.teaser: The president encountered opposition on foreign policy, immigration, and other initiatives during the past week.
cards.body:
President Trump faced pushback on multiple policy fronts from both judicial and legislative branches. Republican members of Congress joined courts in challenging aspects of the administration's agenda on foreign policy and immigration matters.

The resistance marks a notable week of friction between the White House and other government institutions. Both legal challenges and legislative opposition created obstacles for the administration's efforts to implement its policy priorities across several issue areas.

cards.headline: SpaceX Lands $30 Billion Google Cloud Computing Deal
cards.teaser: Google agreed to pay SpaceX nearly $1 billion monthly for computing capacity, marking one of the largest cloud infrastructure contracts ahead of SpaceX's planned public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX secured a $30 billion agreement to provide Google with computing capacity for artificial intelligence operations, with Google paying approximately $920 million per month to lease infrastructure at data centers operated by xAI, according to reports. The multi-year contract represents one of the largest cloud computing deals disclosed publicly and comes as SpaceX prepares for an initial public offering.

The arrangement follows a similar agreement between Google and Anthropic, another AI company, suggesting major technology firms are racing to secure computing resources for AI development. The deal positions SpaceX's infrastructure business as a significant revenue source beyond its rocket and satellite operations, potentially boosting the company's valuation ahead of its planned stock market debut.

hero.headline: Israeli Soldiers Kill Seven-Month-Old Palestinian Baby in West Bank
hero.body:
Israeli police and military forces shot and killed four members of a Palestinian family in the occupied West Bank, including two young children, according to Palestinian health officials and witness accounts.

Mohammed, five, and Othman, seven, who was blind and had special needs, were killed along with their parents, Waad Bani Odeh, 35, and Ali Bani Odeh, 37. The family was returning home to Tamoun after a Ramadan shopping trip late Saturday when undercover Israeli forces opened fire on their vehicle without warning. All four family members were shot in the head and face. Ali, who was driving, was also shot in the chest and left hand.

Two older brothers survived the attack. Khaled, 11, told Reuters that he heard his mother crying and his father praying before the gunfire stopped. He said Israeli forces then dragged him from the wreckage, beat and kicked him, and taunted him about his family's deaths. One of the Israeli forces told him "we killed dogs," Khaled said.

The family had traveled to nearby Nablus to buy clothes for Eid, the celebration marking the end of Ramadan. Both surviving boys sustained shrapnel wounds to the head and eye.

Israeli police said the forces opened fire after perceiving an immediate threat when the vehicle accelerated. The operation was aimed at arresting suspects believed involved in militant activity, according to a police statement. Israeli authorities declined to comment on what threat was posed by unarmed parents and children, or whether the shooting violated rules of engagement. The circumstances remain under review.

Palestinian health officials and the ministry of foreign affairs characterized the killings as an extrajudicial execution. The ministry said such incidents reflect a broader systematic campaign against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

The shooting came hours after Israeli settlers killed Amir Moatasem Odeh, 28, in another West Bank location. His father was stabbed and hospitalized with serious injuries.

The deaths are part of an escalating pattern of violence in the occupied West Bank. Since the last indictment of Israeli forces for a homicide in 2019, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,400 people, including over 320 children, according to UN figures compiled by Israeli human rights group Yesh Din. In recent weeks alone, Israeli settlers have killed six civilians during incursions into Palestinian villages and grazing land.

The incident has drawn international attention to Israel's military conduct in Palestinian territories. Human rights organizations have repeatedly called for accountability in cases involving civilian casualties.

cards.body:
An Israeli military strike killed three Lebanese army officers shortly after Israel and Hezbollah agreed to a ceasefire. The Israeli military confirmed hitting a vehicle in the incident, which is under review.

Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun condemned the strike as "a flagrant violation to Lebanese sovereignty and international law." The incident raises concerns about the ceasefire's stability, as Israel's military operations in Lebanon have increasingly involved Lebanese state forces alongside its primary focus on combating Hezbollah, an Iran-backed armed group.

cards.headline: China Sends Medical Team to Help Contain Ebola in East Africa
cards.teaser: China deployed medical personnel to the Democratic Republic of Congo as the Ebola outbreak continues to spread.
cards.body:
Chinese medical teams have arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to assist with the Ebola response. The deployment reflects China's positioning as equipped to help combat the outbreak, drawing on its previous experience providing medical assistance during African health crises.

The current outbreak poses serious risks. US CDC modeling projects scenarios ranging from 10,000 to over 20,000 cases, potentially matching the scale of the 2014-2016 West African outbreak that killed more than 11,000 people. The outbreak has crossed into Uganda, raising concerns about wider regional spread.

cards.headline: Colombian Presidential Election Heads to Runoff
cards.teaser: Colombia's presidential race will go to a second round after no candidate secured a majority in the first vote.
cards.body:
Colombia will hold a runoff election for president after the initial round failed to produce a clear winner. The race has been shaped by anti-incumbent sentiment, with a far-right candidate emerging as a major contender alongside a leftist opponent who has sought to appeal to centrist voters by backing away from proposals for a new constitution.

The outcome could significantly affect Colombia's relationship with the United States and policies on environmental protection and fossil fuel development. One of the leading candidates is a U.S. citizen, raising questions about eligibility and dual nationality in Colombian politics. The election comes amid broader regional trends of voters rejecting sitting governments across Latin America.

cards.headline: Pope Leo Begins Week-Long Visit to Spain
cards.teaser: Pope Leo arrived in Spain for a visit focused on migrants and marked by tension with the country's far-right.
cards.body:
Pope Leo arrived in Spain on Saturday for a weeklong visit focused on meeting with migrants and addressing social issues. During the trip, he is expected to encounter opposition from Vox, Spain's far-right party, which has criticized the Catholic Church's positions on migration and other policies.

The visit reflects Leo's emphasis on migration and social justice. It comes as conservative political movements in Spain have increasingly distanced themselves from church leadership on various policy matters, creating tension between traditional Catholic voters and the institutional church.

cards.headline: Iran Says Technical Staff Denied U.S. Visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Iranian officials reported that team technical staff were blocked from entering the United States despite players receiving visas.
cards.body:
Iran said technical staff members for its national team were denied U.S. visas hours after American officials approved entry for the players themselves. The timing of the selective visa denials creates significant logistical challenges for Iran's participation in the World Cup, which is being held in the United States.

The contrasting decisions highlight the diplomatic tensions between the two countries. Iran's ability to field a fully functional team now depends on resolving the visa situation for its support staff before the tournament begins.

cards.headline: Filipino sailors deported from US say they were falsely accused of possessing child exploitation material
cards.teaser: Deported Filipino sailors say they were accused without evidence of possessing child sexual exploitation material, with almost none charged or prosecuted.
cards.body:
NPR investigated cases of Filipino sailors deported from the United States after being accused of possessing child sexual exploitation material. According to the sailors, they faced these accusations without evidence and were removed through expedited deportation procedures.

The investigation found that nearly none of the deported sailors were charged or prosecuted in connection with the accusations that triggered their removal, revealing a pattern of deportations that bypassed typical criminal proceedings associated with child exploitation cases.

cards.headline: Republicans in competitive districts show increased willingness to oppose Trump agenda ahead of midterms
cards.teaser: Congressional Republicans facing tough reelection races are breaking with the Trump administration more frequently as the midterm elections approach.
cards.body:
Vulnerable Republican lawmakers are increasingly willing to vote against elements of the Trump administration's agenda as midterm elections draw closer. The shift reflects growing tensions between the White House and members of Congress representing competitive districts.

Several Republican senators and representatives have cast votes opposing administration priorities in recent weeks. The defections mark a departure from earlier unified support and signal that some lawmakers view independence from the White House as politically advantageous in swing districts.

cards.headline: Israeli airstrikes kill nine in Lebanon including army officers after ceasefire agreement
cards.teaser: Israeli strikes killed nine people including Lebanese army officers after a ceasefire deal, prompting Lebanon's president to call it a violation of sovereignty.
cards.body:
Israeli airstrikes killed nine people in Lebanon, including Lebanese army officers, following a newly implemented ceasefire agreement between the two countries. The Israeli military confirmed it struck a vehicle and said the incident is under review.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned the strike as a flagrant violation of Lebanese sovereignty and international law. The attack occurred shortly after both sides had agreed to ceasefire terms.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St Petersburg in what Russia calls unprecedented attack
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones targeted St Petersburg in an attack that Russian officials described as unprecedented, prompting the city's first wartime shelter-in-place order.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck St Petersburg in what Russian officials called an unprecedented attack on the city. The governor ordered residents to remain indoors—the first such directive since the war began. St Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, had not previously experienced drone attacks of this scale.

The strikes prompted President Vladimir Putin to announce plans to strengthen Russia's air defenses. The attacks reached deep into Russian territory and overshadowed Putin's showcase economic forum in his hometown.

cards.headline: Three British men plead guilty to killing Canadian restaurant owner over unpaid bill
cards.teaser: A British man admitted to manslaughter while his father and uncle pleaded guilty to being accessories in the death of a Canadian restaurant owner.
cards.body:
Robert Evans Jr has pleaded guilty to manslaughter in the death of Sharif Rahman, a Canadian restaurant owner. His father and uncle admitted to being accessories to the crime.

The killing arose from a dispute over an unpaid restaurant bill. Canadian police confirmed the guilty pleas from all three British men involved in the case.

cards.headline: West Ham chairman David Sullivan steps down after serious historical allegations emerge
cards.teaser: David Sullivan resigned as West Ham joint chairman and director with immediate effect after learning of impending publication of serious historic allegations.
cards.body:
David Sullivan has stepped down as joint chairman and director of West Ham United with immediate effect. The club announced his departure after Sullivan learned of upcoming allegations against him that it has described as serious and historical.

Sullivan had held a leadership position at the Premier League club for many years. The specific nature of the allegations has not been made public.

hero.headline: SpaceX Lands $30 Billion Google Cloud Computing Deal
hero.teaser: Google agreed to pay SpaceX nearly $1 billion monthly for computing capacity, marking one of the largest cloud infrastructure contracts ahead of SpaceX's planned public offering.
hero.body:
SpaceX secured a $30 billion agreement to provide Google with computing capacity for artificial intelligence operations, with Google paying approximately $920 million per month to lease infrastructure at data centers operated by xAI, according to reports. The multi-year contract represents one of the largest cloud computing deals disclosed publicly and comes as SpaceX prepares for an initial public offering.

The arrangement follows a similar agreement between Google and Anthropic, another AI company, suggesting major technology firms are racing to secure computing resources for AI development. The deal positions SpaceX's infrastructure business as a significant revenue source beyond its rocket and satellite operations, potentially boosting the company's valuation ahead of its planned stock market debut.

cards.headline: Nasdaq Falls 4.2% in Chip Stock Sell-Off
cards.teaser: The Nasdaq Composite dropped 4.2% on Friday, marking its worst single-day decline since April 2025, as investors sold technology stocks amid concerns about chip.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq Composite dropped 4.2% on Friday, marking its worst single-day decline since April 2025, as investors sold technology stocks amid concerns about chip sector valuations and rising odds of Federal Reserve interest rate increases. The tech-heavy index led broader market losses, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also posting significant declines.

Chip stocks drove the market downturn, with semiconductor companies experiencing what some analysts characterized as a sector-wide sell-off. The decline came as traders reassessed artificial intelligence investment themes that had powered much of the market's gains in recent months. Major technology companies with exposure to chip manufacturing and AI infrastructure saw their shares fall sharply during Friday's trading session.

The market retreat reflected growing concern about Federal Reserve policy direction, with traders increasing their estimates of the likelihood the central bank will raise interest rates in coming months. Higher interest rates typically pressure technology stocks more than other sectors because their valuations depend heavily on future earnings growth, which becomes less attractive when safer investments like bonds offer better returns. The shift in rate expectations followed recent economic data suggesting persistent inflation pressures.

Friday's losses extended a difficult week for the Nasdaq, which posted its worst weekly performance in more than a year according to market data. The S&P 500 also recorded its worst day of 2026 as the selling pressure spread beyond technology stocks to other growth-oriented sectors. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which includes fewer technology companies, declined but held up better than the other major indexes.

The market turbulence comes at a time when technology valuations had reached elevated levels, particularly among companies tied to artificial intelligence development and deployment. Investors had bid up chip stocks and AI-related companies throughout much of 2025 and early 2026, creating concerns about whether share prices had outpaced underlying business fundamentals. Friday's sell-off suggested some investors were taking profits or repositioning portfolios in response to changing interest rate expectations and valuation concerns.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Discusses Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: President Trump and lawmakers across the political spectrum are exploring proposals for the government to take ownership stakes in artificial intelligence companies including OpenAI and Anthropic.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is exploring a potential profit-sharing arrangement with artificial intelligence companies, with meetings planned for the following week. President Trump expressed support for U.S. government ownership in AI firms, calling it "a beautiful thing." Meanwhile, Senator Bernie Sanders introduced legislation proposing a 50% government stock position in OpenAI and Anthropic through a sovereign wealth fund.

The discussions reflect growing bipartisan interest in public ownership within the AI sector, traditionally dominated by private investment. Trump, Sanders, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have all signaled openness to government participation in AI company ownership, though the specific structures and terms remain under negotiation.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Tops CEO Compensation Rankings
cards.teaser: Musk's pay packages across Tesla and SpaceX placed him at the top of executive compensation lists, as the gap between CEO and worker pay continues to widen in corporate America.
cards.body:
Elon Musk tops the rankings of highest-paid chief executives, with compensation packages at Tesla and SpaceX totaling over $1 trillion, according to executive compensation analysis. His total compensation far exceeds that of other corporate leaders.

Executive compensation continues to accelerate while typical worker pay growth lags behind, widening the pay gap between top executives and rank-and-file employees at major corporations. Musk's compensation structure at SpaceX, developed following disputes over his Tesla pay package, is influencing how companies design executive incentive arrangements.

cards.headline: Executives Turn to AI Twins for Meetings and Email
cards.teaser: CEOs and professors are deploying artificial intelligence versions of themselves to handle routine meetings and answer questions as a productivity strategy.
cards.body:
Business executives and academics are creating AI-powered digital versions of themselves to attend meetings and respond to questions on their behalf, according to reports on emerging workplace practices. The AI twins are programmed to mimic the communication style and decision-making patterns of the individuals they represent, handling routine interactions while the actual person focuses on other priorities.

The practice has gained traction among CEOs and Harvard professors as a way to manage overwhelming schedules and communication demands. Proponents view the technology as a productivity tool that allows them to scale their availability, though the approach raises questions about authentic human interaction in professional settings and the boundaries of acceptable delegation.

cards.headline: Target Recalls Baby Wipes Over Bacterial Contamination Risk
cards.teaser: Target voluntarily recalled two types of baby wipes after discovering potential contamination with bacteria that can cause life-threatening infections.
cards.body:
Target issued a voluntary recall of two types of baby wipes sold under its store brands due to potential contamination with bacteria capable of causing serious infections. The company warned the bacteria could pose life-threatening health risks, particularly to vulnerable populations including infants and people with weakened immune systems.

The recall affects specific lots of Target-branded baby wipes sold at stores nationwide. Target advised customers who purchased the affected products to stop using them immediately and return them to stores for refunds. The company did not disclose how many units were affected or whether any illnesses had been reported in connection with the contaminated wipes.

cards.headline: Screwworm Outbreak Threatens Texas Cattle Industry
cards.teaser: Texas ranchers face the possibility of a screwworm fly outbreak while drought conditions force early cattle sales due to insufficient grazing grass.
cards.body:
Cattle ranchers in Texas are facing a screwworm outbreak that has prompted Canada to ban imports of Texas cattle. The parasite, transmitted by flies that lay eggs in open wounds, can cause severe livestock damage and death. A second infected calf was identified in the state, leading Texas to declare a disaster over the outbreak.

The screwworm threat compounds existing challenges for ranchers already struggling with drought conditions. Insufficient grass has forced many to send animals to market earlier than planned, adding economic pressure to an industry now confronting the risk of rapid parasite spread through herds.

hero.headline: AI finds more than 800 undocumented objects in 35 years of Hubble telescope images
hero.body:
A machine learning system has identified more than 800 previously undocumented objects hidden within 35 years of images captured by the Hubble Space Telescope, revealing that one of astronomy's most celebrated archives still contains undiscovered phenomena waiting to be found.

The artificial intelligence system processed the vast collection of Hubble observations accumulated since the telescope's launch in 1990. These newly identified objects were present in images that astronomers had already examined, indicating that traditional human analysis had overlooked them despite previous reviews.

The Hubble archive contains millions of observations gathered across more than three decades of continuous operation. While professional astronomers have studied numerous images extensively, the sheer volume of data makes it impractical for researchers to manually review everything comprehensively. Machine learning systems can analyze images at speeds far exceeding human capabilities and can identify patterns or unusual features that might be missed during conventional examination.

The discovery demonstrates the lasting scientific importance of long-term space missions and highlights how artificial intelligence can extract previously hidden information from existing datasets. Throughout its operational lifetime, Hubble has captured imagery of distant galaxies, nebulae, star clusters, and various other celestial objects and phenomena. Some of the newly discovered objects may have remained unidentified in the archive for years or even decades before the AI system brought them to light.

The findings suggest that other major astronomical collections may similarly harbor undiscovered objects. Space agencies and research organizations maintain extensive archives of images from multiple telescopes and space missions. Implementing comparable AI techniques across these diverse datasets could uncover additional objects and phenomena that have remained hidden despite supposedly thorough earlier analysis.

This work illustrates a broader trend in modern astronomy where machine learning augments human expertise rather than replacing it. The combination of human scientific knowledge and artificial intelligence's pattern recognition abilities creates powerful tools for exploring massive volumes of scientific data. As telescopes continue operating and generating new observations, and as archives from past missions remain scientifically valuable, AI systems will increasingly help researchers identify discoveries that might otherwise escape notice.

The application of these techniques could accelerate the pace of astronomical discovery and help maximize the scientific return from expensive space missions. It also suggests that many important findings may still be waiting within data that scientists have already collected, offering research value that extends far beyond the original mission objectives.

cards.headline: Scientists detect wind from Milky Way's supermassive black hole after 50-year search
cards.teaser: Astronomers found evidence of wind emanating from Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way galaxy.
cards.body:
Researchers discovered wind coming from Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, ending a search that lasted five decades. The findings show that even relatively quiet black holes generate winds, not just the active ones that consume large amounts of matter.

The discovery required new observations and analysis techniques to detect the wind signature. Black holes at the centers of galaxies can drive powerful outflows that affect their surrounding environments. The detection confirms that this phenomenon occurs even in less active black holes like the one at the Milky Way's core.

cards.headline: Ancient microbes frozen with Ötzi the Iceman still growing after 5,300 years
cards.teaser: Microorganisms preserved alongside the 5,300-year-old mummy can still reproduce, researchers found.
cards.body:
Scientists discovered that some microbes frozen with Ötzi, the 5,300-year-old mummy found in the Alps, remain viable and can still grow. The finding raises questions about the boundaries between preserved biological specimens and living ecosystems.

The microorganisms survived millennia of freezing temperatures alongside the human remains. Their continued viability challenges traditional classifications of archaeological finds and suggests that ancient ice can preserve living organisms far longer than previously understood.

cards.headline: Spain prepares for first of three upcoming solar eclipses this summer
cards.teaser: The country will host multiple eclipse viewing opportunities, with the first event scheduled for August.
cards.body:
Spain will experience three solar eclipses in the near future, with the first arriving this summer in August. The August eclipse offers multiple viewing locations across the country, including major vacation destinations and vineyard regions. Experts have warned viewers about potential risks from sun exposure, crowds, and summer heat during the events.

One of the eclipses will be the longest total solar eclipse of the century, lasting six minutes and 23 seconds of complete darkness. The duration makes it an exceptional astronomical event. Authorities are preparing for increased tourism as eclipse watchers travel to Spain for optimal viewing conditions.

cards.headline: Microsoft AI executive says split from OpenAI enabled pursuit of superintelligence
cards.teaser: The company's AI chief stated that separation from its former partner allowed Microsoft to focus on advanced AI development.
cards.body:
Microsoft's AI division head stated that the company gained freedom to pursue superintelligence following changes in its relationship with OpenAI. The remarks were made during Microsoft Build 2026, the company's annual developer conference.

The partnership between Microsoft and OpenAI has deteriorated according to multiple sources. Microsoft has invested billions in OpenAI over several years but is now pursuing a more independent path for its AI research and product development.

cards.headline: Square Enix announces Final Fantasy VII Revelation to complete remake trilogy in 2027
cards.teaser: The third installment in the Final Fantasy VII remake series will launch in spring 2027.
cards.body:
Square Enix has officially unveiled Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the final installment of its remake trilogy. The game will launch simultaneously across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2 in spring 2027. A first trailer debuted at Summer Game Fest Live.

The trilogy reimagines the original 1997 Final Fantasy VII across three full-length games. Revelation will feature an evolved open world that builds on systems introduced in the previous title, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth.

cards.headline: Capcom reveals Resident Evil: Veronica remake for 2027 release
cards.teaser: The remake of Code: Veronica will launch next year for multiple platforms including Nintendo Switch 2.
cards.body:
Capcom announced Resident Evil: Veronica, a remake of the 2000 game Resident Evil Code: Veronica, during Summer Game Fest 2026. The company set a 2027 release date for the title. The game will be available on Nintendo Switch 2 along with other platforms.

The announcement was part of multiple reveals from Capcom at the showcase event. The original Code: Veronica released for Dreamcast and later other platforms. The remake continues Capcom's strategy of updating classic Resident Evil titles with modern graphics and gameplay systems.

hero.headline: Knicks take 2-0 lead in NBA Finals after Wembanyama turnover seals Game 2 win
hero.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs 105-104 in Game 2 of the NBA Finals, taking a commanding 2-0 series lead back to Madison Square Garden. The Knicks became only the third team to win the first two games of an NBA Finals on the road, joining the 1993 Chicago Bulls and 1995 Houston Rockets.

The game came down to the final seconds, with Jalen Brunson sinking the go-ahead free throw with 9.5 seconds remaining after a costly turnover by Spurs star Victor Wembanyama. Moments later, Wembanyama's clean look from the elbow at the buzzer caromed off the back rim, securing the victory for New York.

The turnover that sealed the game involved Wembanyama passing the ball into teammate Stephon Castle's back before the Knicks capitalized on the miscue. Stephon Castle later explained the unusual play, while Wembanyama expressed regret over the critical mistake that contributed to San Antonio's defeat. The Spurs' young star had been trying to compensate for his blunder but overextended in his efforts, ultimately helping secure the Knicks' win.

Brunson played a pivotal role in the Knicks' victory, making key plays in the crucial final moments. Karl-Anthony Towns carried the team on both ends of the floor, helping New York hold off a Spurs rush in the second half. Josh Hart emphasized the team's focus on continued improvement despite holding a commanding series advantage.

The Knicks benefited from favorable calls and executed important plays down the stretch to secure the one-point victory. The team's hot shooting and strong defense have defined their playoff run, with the franchise now just two wins away from capturing its first NBA championship in more than fifty years.

The Spurs face the challenge of overcoming a two-game deficit as they prepare for the critical Game 3 matchup in New York. San Antonio must regroup after the difficult loss and find ways to slow down the Knicks' dynamic offense while limiting their own turnovers in high-pressure situations. The young Spurs roster will need to replicate the depth and balance that led to their Game 7 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder in the previous round.

Security measures at Madison Square Garden will include enhanced protocols for Game 3, with a ban on all bags due to the expected attendance of former President Donald Trump, who accepted an invitation to attend the game. Ticket prices for the Finals games at MSG have reached $9,000 on the secondary market, drawing significant public attention to the cost of attending the championship series. The Knicks now take their red-hot form home, where they will attempt to move within one win of the championship title.

cards.headline: Andreeva and Chwalinska to meet in French Open final
cards.teaser: Mirra Andreeva will face Maja Chwalinska in the French Open final, marking one of the most unexpected championship matches in recent tournament history.
cards.body:
Mirra Andreeva and Maja Chwalinska will compete for the French Open women's singles title on Saturday in one of the tournament's most unlikely finals. Both unseeded players have demonstrated impressive form throughout the draw, dropping only one set each on their path to the championship match.

Andreeva reached the final by defeating Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk in the semi-finals, snapping her opponent's 17-match winning streak. Chwalinska has pulled off several upsets, including victories over Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen and multiple seeded players: Elise Mertens, Anna Kalinskaya, and Diana Shnaider.

cards.headline: Knights and opponent tied 1-1 as Stanley Cup Finals shift to Las Vegas
cards.teaser: The Stanley Cup playoffs continue with Games 3 and 4 moving to Las Vegas after the series was tied at one game apiece.
cards.body:
The Stanley Cup Finals stands tied at 1-1 as the series relocates to Las Vegas for the next two games. Both teams split the opening games before the venue change.

John Tortorella, hired with just eight games remaining in the regular season, has guided the Knights through key decisions in the playoffs. The veteran coach made strategic adjustments that helped turn the team's fortunes around during the postseason run.

cards.headline: Belmont Stakes field set for race at Saratoga
cards.teaser: The horses competing in the 2026 Belmont Stakes have been confirmed, with the race taking place at Saratoga this year.
cards.body:
The field for the 2026 Belmont Stakes is complete, with multiple horses entered in the third leg of thoroughbred racing's Triple Crown. The race will be held at Saratoga rather than its traditional Belmont Park location.

Post times and television coverage have been scheduled for the Belmont Stakes racing weekend. Oddsmakers have established favorites for the race, while handicappers who correctly predicted four of the past eight winners have shared their selections for this year's running.

cards.headline: Patten and Heliovaara lose French Open men's doubles final
cards.teaser: Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara were defeated in the French Open men's doubles final.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Henry Patten and his Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara were defeated in the French Open men's doubles final. They lost to Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos at Roland Garros.

The loss prevented Patten and Heliovaara from claiming the Grand Slam title in their first major final together.

cards.headline: India names 15-year-old Sooryavanshi to T20 squad
cards.teaser: Fifteen-year-old batting prospect Vaibhav Sooryavanshi received his first international call-up to India's T20 squad for tours of England and Ireland.
cards.body:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, has been selected for India's T20 squad for the upcoming tours of England and Ireland. The teenage opener earned his maiden call-up to the national team following an impressive IPL season.

Sooryavanshi's performances in the Indian Premier League caught selectors' attention, with the young batter accumulating 776 runs at a strike rate of 237.30 and winning the tournament's most valuable player award. If he debuts, he is set to become India's youngest international player since Sachin Tendulkar.

cards.headline: World Cup predictions map out tournament path for 48 teams
cards.teaser: Analysts have predicted results for every match in the 48-team FIFA World Cup rather than selecting only a tournament winner.
cards.body:
A comprehensive World Cup prediction project has forecast the outcome of each match in the expanded 48-team tournament, revealing not just a predicted champion but the complete path to victory.

EA's World Cup simulation has continued its impressive track record, successfully predicting the winner in each of the last four World Cups. The video game publisher's model provides detailed match-by-match forecasts for the tournament.

hero.headline: British Actor Anthony Head Dies at 72
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the acclaimed British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications related to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said.

Head's portrayal of Giles, the school librarian and mentor to Sarah Michelle Gellar's title character, became iconic in television history. The role established him as a respected figure in both British and American entertainment. After the show ended in 2003, Head continued working steadily across multiple projects and genres.

Beyond Buffy, Head's career demonstrated remarkable versatility. He appeared in the BBC sketch comedy series Little Britain, where he played a prime minister constantly fawned over by a flirtatious assistant. He also took roles in the fantasy series Merlin and more recently featured in the Apple TV+ series Ted Lasso, where he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion and developed praised on-screen chemistry with co-creator Jason Sudeikis.

Head's earlier work included film roles in The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie. He also gained significant public recognition in the 1980s through a long-running series of Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements that followed the slow-burn romance between two characters.

Before achieving international fame, Head built a strong stage career. He starred in the 1978 West End revival of Godspell alongside Su Pollard and later performed in productions including the original West End production of the Abba musical Chess in 1988, where he played Freddie Trumper. He also took the lead role as Dr Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show.

Born in Camden, London, Head came from an artistic family. His father founded Verity Films as a documentary filmmaker, while his mother was an actor who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother also pursued an acting career. In the early 1980s, Head sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box and appeared on their 1986 debut album.

During his five years in Los Angeles filming Buffy, Head maintained a long-distance relationship with his partner Sarah and their two young daughters in England. He described traveling home every three to four weeks whenever the production schedule allowed.

His daughters emphasized that Head considered himself fortunate to work with exceptional talent across his lengthy career. "We know his legacy will live on in the shows he was a part of and in the audiences that love them," they said.

cards.headline: Welsh Singer Duffy to Perform First Concert in 15 Years
cards.teaser: The Welsh singer has scheduled her first live performance after stepping away from public life following a sexual assault.
cards.body:
Duffy has announced her first live concert following a 15-year absence from performing. The Welsh singer stepped away from public life after experiencing a sexual assault.

Her return to the stage marks a significant moment after years away from the spotlight.

cards.headline: Royals Attend Wedding of Princess Anne's Son Peter Phillips
cards.teaser: Peter Phillips, the son of Princess Anne, married NHS nurse Harriet Sperling in a ceremony attended by members of the royal family.
cards.body:
Members of the British royal family gathered to celebrate the wedding of Peter Phillips and Harriet Sperling. Phillips, the oldest grandchild of the late Queen Elizabeth II, married Sperling, an NHS nurse.

King Charles attended the ceremony, while Kate Middleton wore a blush-colored Roland Mouret dress to the celebration.

cards.headline: Toy Story 5 Used Decoy Version to Hide Taylor Swift Role
cards.teaser: Pixar created a fake version of Toy Story 5 to keep Taylor Swift's involvement secret from most of the production crew.
cards.body:
Visual effects supervisor Thomas Jordan revealed that Pixar made a decoy version of Toy Story 5 to conceal Taylor Swift's participation in the film. The crew working on the movie did not learn about Swift's involvement until last week, Jordan said. Swift performs a song in the film titled "I Knew It, I Knew You."

The elaborate secrecy measures kept Swift's role hidden throughout production. Jordan disclosed this information on Friday, explaining the lengths the studio went to in order to maintain the surprise for audiences and even the production team itself.

cards.headline: Madonna Criticizes Phone Use at Concert Film Premiere
cards.teaser: Madonna urged audiences to put away their phones during a screening and discussion of her new concert film at the Beacon Theater.
cards.body:
Madonna appeared at the Beacon Theater on Manhattan's Upper West Side for the premiere of Confessions II The Film. During the event, she addressed the audience about technology's impact on live entertainment experiences, telling attendees to put their phones down and connect with the performance.

The screening was followed by a question and answer session with Madonna and the directing duo TORSO, consisting of David Toro and Solomon. The premiere drew a dedicated group of fans to the historic venue on the Upper West Side.

cards.headline: Jodie Foster Recalls Taxi Driver Set Memory at 50th Anniversary
cards.teaser: Jodie Foster shared memories from filming Taxi Driver at the film's 50th anniversary reunion at the Tribeca Festival.
cards.body:
Jodie Foster reflected on her iconic role as Iris in Taxi Driver during the film's 50th anniversary celebration at the Tribeca Festival. Joined by director Martin Scorsese, actor Robert De Niro, and screenwriter Paul Schrader, Foster shared memories from the 1976 production.

Foster recalled a particularly amusing moment when Scorsese and De Niro taught her how to unzip a fly for a scene. The two were so nervous about the instruction that they couldn't stop giggling throughout the exchange—a memory that has remained with Foster all these years.

cards.headline: Kerry Washington and Tony Goldwyn Discuss Scandal Characters' Future
cards.teaser: The former Scandal co-stars spoke about their characters' relationship and fan reactions at a reunion discussion.
cards.body:
Kerry Washington and Tony Goldwyn recently reflected on their characters from the Shonda Rhimes series "Scandal," which ran from 2012 to 2018. Washington portrayed Olivia Pope, a Washington D.C. fixer, while Goldwyn played President Fitzgerald Grant. The actors shared insights into their on-screen relationship, which fans had dubbed "Olitz."

According to the conversation, Olivia and Fitz remain together in the show's universe and are currently attending couples therapy. Their relationship was a major storyline throughout the series, despite the complications arising from Fitz's marriage and presidential position. Fans have also encouraged both actors to run for president themselves.

hero.headline: Trump floats federal stake in AI companies to share profits with public
hero.body:
President Trump has proposed that the U.S. government acquire small ownership stakes in major artificial intelligence companies, allowing the American public to benefit financially from what he expects will become trillion-dollar enterprises.

"There's something very interesting about it, where it almost becomes a partnership with the American public," Trump said to reporters aboard Air Force One. "It's like you make them [partners] in this revolution. It would be a beautiful thing. ... It would make 'em rich."

Trump indicated he has raised the concept during recent meetings with AI company leaders, describing their reactions as surprised. The idea would represent a significant shift from traditional government-industry relationships, establishing direct financial connections between federal authorities and private technology firms developing artificial intelligence.

The proposal aligns with existing advocacy from influential figures in the tech sector. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has previously championed similar arrangements. This week, Senator Bernie Sanders revived the discussion by proposing that the public receive a direct ownership stake in major AI companies through a one-time 50 percent tax paid in stock.

The concept raises several unresolved questions about practical implementation. Details remain unclear regarding how ownership stakes would be structured, what percentage of companies the government would acquire, and the mechanisms for distributing any resulting profits to taxpayers. Trump has not specified whether he would pursue the idea through executive action or request congressional approval.

The timing of Trump's suggestion comes as artificial intelligence companies have attracted enormous investment and as policymakers grapple with regulating the rapidly advancing technology. The notion of federal ownership in private AI firms introduces potential complications, particularly regarding the government's multiple roles as investor, regulator, and national security overseer of the industry.

Federal ownership stakes could create significant conflicts of interest. The government would need to balance its financial interests in company growth and profitability against its regulatory responsibilities and obligations to protect national security. These competing interests might affect policy decisions related to AI development, safety standards, and international competitiveness.

The proposal also raises governance questions about how the government would exercise its ownership stake and whether federal representatives would serve on company boards. Such involvement could influence strategic decisions at some of the world's most important technology companies.

Industry observers note that the concept differs from traditional government support mechanisms like grants or tax incentives. It would tie public finances directly to the success of specific private companies, creating unprecedented arrangements in the technology sector.

As AI technology continues advancing rapidly and companies in the space command increasing valuations, the conversation about how the public should benefit from this growth appears likely to intensify. Trump's public endorsement of the idea suggests it may receive serious consideration within his administration going forward.

cards.headline: Trump expands TrumpRx platform with 160 additional prescription drugs
cards.teaser: The administration added over 100 medications to its direct-to-consumer drug program, bringing the total to more than 800.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that the TrumpRx platform will add 160 prescription medications at discounted prices. The expansion marks the second increase to the direct-to-consumer drug initiative in two months.

The administration's platform now offers more than 800 prescription drugs through TrumpRx.gov. Trump made the announcement publicly, emphasizing the highly discounted pricing available through the program for consumers purchasing medications directly.

cards.headline: May jobs report shows 172,000 positions added, beating forecasts
cards.teaser: The U.S. economy exceeded expectations with steady unemployment as the midterm elections approach.
cards.body:
The U.S. added 172,000 jobs in May while the unemployment rate remained at 4.3%, demonstrating resilience in the labor market despite rising inflation and regional economic uncertainty stemming from Middle East conflicts.

However, broader market sentiment turned negative on Friday as stocks fell sharply. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index dropped 4%—its largest single-day decline in over a year—following a sell-off in AI chip stocks. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones also declined 2.6% and 1.3% respectively.

cards.headline: Supreme Court nears decisions on birthright citizenship and presidential power
cards.teaser: The court will rule in coming weeks on cases affecting immigration policy and executive authority over federal officials.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court is preparing to issue decisions in several major cases before its summer recess. The pending rulings include challenges to birthright citizenship policies, immigration enforcement, and the extent of presidential power to remove federal employees from their positions.

The cases represent some of the court's most significant decisions of the term. The rulings will affect constitutional questions surrounding immigration policy and the separation of powers between branches of government. The court typically completes its work by late June or early July.

cards.headline: Cornyn backs away from Trump highway naming bill after primary defeat
cards.teaser: The Texas senator signaled the legislation to rename U.S. Highway 287 may no longer be a priority following his loss in the GOP runoff.
cards.body:
Sen. John Cornyn indicated he is stepping back from legislation that would designate a Texas highway after President Trump. Cornyn introduced the bill in May to rename U.S. Highway 287 as Interstate 47, but suggested the measure is no longer high on his agenda.

The shift comes after Cornyn lost his GOP Senate primary runoff election last month. The Texas Republican had proposed the highway designation as part of his legislative efforts, but his comments suggest the bill will not receive the same level of attention following his electoral defeat.

cards.headline: Trump agenda faces resistance from courts and Republican lawmakers
cards.teaser: The president encountered opposition on foreign policy, immigration, and other initiatives during the past week.
cards.body:
President Trump faced pushback on multiple policy fronts from both judicial and legislative branches. Republican members of Congress joined courts in challenging aspects of the administration's agenda on foreign policy and immigration matters.

The resistance marks a notable week of friction between the White House and other government institutions. Both legal challenges and legislative opposition created obstacles for the administration's efforts to implement its policy priorities across several issue areas.

cards.headline: Election officials increasingly rely on local police for security
cards.teaser: Law enforcement agencies have taken on expanded roles in protecting election workers and polling sites since 2020.
cards.body:
Local police departments are playing a larger role in securing elections as tensions surrounding voting have intensified. Election officials have turned to law enforcement agencies for support in protecting staff and ensuring safe voting operations.

The shift began after the 2020 election and has continued to grow. Local authorities have increased coordination with police to address security concerns at polling locations and election offices as political tensions have risen around voting procedures.
